name: Sarah
description: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: Abram and Nahor took them wives; Sarai was barren; and Terah took Abram, Lot, and Sarai and went forth from Ur toward Canaan. No attraction language, and what follows immediately is that they moved to another country and she did not buck. You marry a whole family: father-in-law, daughter-in-law, nephew, and all the risk and hardship shared.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Sarai was around the same age as Abram, about ten years apart, and she was still a very fair woman to look upon in her sixties.

A famine sent Abram into Egypt, as it would send Jacob later, and the Lord plagued Pharaoh's house over Sarai; here Abraham acquired Hagar, and here, by Josephus, he taught the Egyptians arithmetic and astronomy and confuted their divided customs.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

points: The Lord plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, and Pharaoh sent Abram away with his wife and all that he had. The Most High protected the household of Abram in Egypt.
Hagar was Sarai's Egyptian handmaid, from the servants Pharaoh gave in Genesis 12:16.
Sarai, restrained from bearing, gave her maid to Abram that she might obtain children by her.
Sarai laid the wrong on Abram, and Abram answered, Behold, thy maid is in thy hand. He did not say my wife; he had no attachment to Hagar. His sole purpose was the seed, not multiple wives.
Abram kept the laws of the Most High. Do not use this account to justify taking multiple wives; the purpose here was the promised inheritance, and Sarai dealt with her maid as mistress over her.
Sarai's name was changed to Sarah, and she shall be a mother of nations; those are the same nations of the covenant, and she and Abraham had one child together, Isaac.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

points: Abraham fell on his face and laughed in his heart: shall a child be born to a hundred year old man, and Sarah bear at ninety? The Most High read his thought and named the child from it: Isaac means he will laugh.

note.label: Genesis 17: The Covenant Sealed in the Flesh

points: And Abraham hastened into the tent unto Sarah, and said, Make ready quickly three measures of fine meal, knead it, and make cakes upon the hearth. And Abraham ran unto the herd. So imagine, you see these three men, you want them to come to your house, you are telling your wife, get food, get everything, get ready. Three men just came. These men are men of the Lord.
Abraham hastened to serve them. He commanded his household; he told Sarah, Make ready quickly. That is the level of his hospitality and his leadership.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

points: And they said unto him, Where is Sarah thy wife? And he said, Behold, in the tent. And he said, I will certainly return unto thee according to the time of life; and, lo, Sarah thy wife shall have a son. And Sarah heard it in the tent door, which was behind him. He is talking with the men. She is listening in the tent, like, what is going on? What is all this commotion for? What are you all talking about?

Now Abraham and Sarah were old and well stricken in age. They are almost a hundred years old. And look what the men of the Lord tell them. And it ceased to be with Sarah after the manner of women. She cannot have no baby at a hundred.
Sarah was barren from the beginning and it had ceased to be with her after the manner of women; she laughed within herself at the promise of a son.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

points: Therefore Sarah laughed within herself. So she was eavesdropping. They were not talking to her. They were talking to her husband and she was being nosy. It says she laughed within herself. She did not burst out laughing.

And the Lord said unto Abraham, Wherefore did Sarah laugh, saying, Shall I of a surety bear a child, which am old? Remember, it says she laughed inside. And the man said, why is your wife laughing? She was outside the tent not minding her business. And they told them, check your wife, she is laughing. Because you all get mad when we tell you all stuff about your wives in here. And they did it right in front of our face. It said that she laughed within herself. She did not tell those men that.
Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.

Is any thing too hard for the Lord? The barren woman is made a joyful mother of children. Through faith Sarah received strength to conceive when she was past age, and Abraham, as good as dead at a hundred, staggered not at the promise but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what He had promised He was able to perform.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

points: Then Sarah denied, saying, I laughed not. She said, I did not laugh. Like she was trying to say the angels lied on her. For she was afraid. And he said, Nay; but thou didst laugh. So you did laugh.

So the lie that Sarah told — I do not want to say a white lie, because it is still a lie, but she was afraid. She lied out of fear. Like Deacon Malachi said, in one of the schools we had a girl lie on one of the men. We had to go back and rewind the tape. She said that he touched her, and when we rewound the tape he was nowhere in her vicinity. That is the type of lie that Deacon Malachi is talking about. That is a wicked, despicable woman. When we rewound the tape, it was nothing like how she was saying. So you know that a seed of evil has been planted inside of you, if you sat down and you thought that up: I am going to tell them he touched me even though he did not touch me. And there are cameras all over to prove her wrong. That is a wicked person.
The Lord answered the thought she never spoke: Wherefore did Sarah laugh? She denied it out of fear, and He said, Nay, but thou didst laugh. The Most High sees what is within the mind.

note.label: Genesis 18: The Promise of Isaac and the Cry of Sodom

points: Abraham said again, She is my sister, as he had done entering Egypt, for fear the men of the place would kill him for his wife's sake; Sarah was still that fair to look upon even at ninety.
Behind the scenes the Lord had fast closed up all the wombs of the house of Abimelech because of Sarah; when Abraham prayed, God healed them.

The thing was very grievous in Abraham's sight because of his son; every man loves his kids. So the Most High had to intervene: Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. The righteous seed, the prophets, come through Isaac. And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed: do not worry about your son, he is going to be all right.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: It was grievous to Abraham because he loved his firstborn, but God said, Hearken unto her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Sarah was on point; Isaac is the child of the promise.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

points: Sarah lived an hundred and seven and twenty years, and died in Kirjatharba, the same is Hebron, in the land of Canaan; Abraham came to mourn and to weep for her.

Being not weak in faith, Abraham considered not his own body now dead at about an hundred years old, neither the deadness of Sarah's womb at ninety; he staggered not at the promise through unbelief, but was strong in faith, fully persuaded that what God had promised he was able to perform. He never saw his seed become the stars, but he believed it, meek and submissive like Moses, and therefore it was imputed to him for righteousness.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: Being in subjection unto their own husbands: even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. That you are not afraid to submit, that you are not afraid that those things will run you errant. How many of you have just been unyielding in certain situations. And yes, it does not make the things the husband might be doing right, but it does make you right if you stay in that lane with God. And then if you believe and you fear God and you have that confidence in him, then he will show you a path forward to have reconciliation in that division that is in your house.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife
